newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS -Yen vols shoot up as spot loses ground.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS -Yen vols shoot up as spot loses ground.

text.p: Implied volatilities in dollar/yen options jumped by European midday after the yen gave way against the dollar in the spot market overnight to bring a major target level of 120 yen back into the horizon.

"It looks like the market's slightly short of dollar/yen call options, and so people get nervous when spot goes up putting pressure on 120 (yen) and drive up dollar/yen vols," said James Binney, fund manager at GNI in London.

Spot dollar rose by more then two and a half yen on Thursday and was at 118.50/60 yen at 1125 GMT against 117.80/85 in late European trade yesterday. Yen weakness across the board was the main cause of dollar/yen's strength.

Recent sharp plunges in Asian currencies had heightened worries that the regional foreign exchange turmoil boded ill for the Japanese currency as well, while the temperamental signs of recovery in the Japanese economy increased perceptions that Japan's interest rates were unlikely to rise for some time.

Such moves in spot caused a flurry of dollar call buying, with one-month dollar/yen volatilities quoted at 12.20/50 percent against 10.60/80 in late Europe on Thursday. with Traders said they were traded as high as 12.55 percent earlier on Friday.
"There's been talk that there are quite a few buyers of overnight dollar calls at as high as 120 yen," said one trader at a Japanese bank here.
"In this case 'overnight' is Monday, and we do have the (Japanese) July trade data coming out over the weekend so I suppose people are taking that into consideration as well," he said.

There was also a sharp turnaround in demand for calls and puts on Friday, with dollar calls now taking the lead. Dollar/yen 25-delta risk reversals showed demand in favour of dollar calls at 0.3/0.6 against 0.1/0.4 in favour of yen calls on Thursday.
The latest perceptions in the spot market were seen as likely to keep dollar/yen calls well bid for some time.

"There's a general trend of Asian currencies showing a lot of volatility at the moment, and as a result, their weakening makes the yen look rather overvalued relative to all those currencies, and the yen needs to weaken for competitive reasons," GNI's Binney said.

"Most of those east Asian currencies were effectively pegged to the dollar, and now they're falling relative to the dollar. So the issue has more to do with dollar/yen rather than mark/yen, though obviously it will have an impact on all the yen crosses," he said.
Spot yen had dropped to its lowest in two weeks against the mark on Friday and was quoted at 64.36/39 per mark, down from 63.87/90 late on Thursday.

Mark/yen vols rose accordingly, with one-month quoted at 11.30/80 against yesterday's 10.90/20. Risk reversals showed put and call demand at around par compared with 0.3/0.7 in favour of mark puts on Thursday.
Meanwhile, dollar/mark vols edged lower as spot dollar ticked higher against the mark after its slide earlier in the week. One-month vols were at 10.75/00 percent against 10.90/00.
Sterling volatilities languished as spot settled down against the dollar and mark, with one-month sterling/mark vols at 11.70/10 against 12.30/70 and cable vols at 10.00/30 against 10.20/60.
